title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous pages): U/S is a relative curve, possibly affine, i.e. a complement of a divisor in a smooth proper curve. K is the function field of S, and s is a point of S of codimension 1. Grothendieck takes the (non-strict) henselization Õ of O_{S,s}, with fraction field K̃ and residue field k = k(s), and writes π = π_1(U_{K̄}).

He has the two homotopy exact sequences
- 1→π→E_{U_K̃}→E_K̃=Gal(K̄/K̃)→1
- 1→π→E_{U_Õ}→E_Õ≅Gal(k̄/k)→1.

The kernel of E_K̃→E_Õ is the inertia group I_{s'}, which he identifies with T (the Tate-type module Ẑ(1)). Since the map on π is the identity, the snake lemma gives two facts:
- E_{U_K̃}→E_{U_Õ} is surjective.
- Its kernel maps isomorphically onto I_{s'}≅T.
This gives the 3×3 diagram (*).

A K-rational point f_K of U_K gives a section of E_{U_K}→E_K. Its restriction to the decomposition group E_K̃≅N_{s'} is the section attached to the corresponding K̃-point f_K̃; this is functoriality of the section map.

Now compose with E_{U_K̃}→E_{U_Õ}. The inertia I≅T goes to the kernel of E_{U_Õ}→E_Õ, i.e. into π. Grothendieck asserts that the resulting map T→π is essentially K_i∘(μ·id_T). Here K_i: T→π is a 'homomorphisme-lacet', the canonical inertia/loop homomorphism at the cusp with index i (a point at infinity of the fibre), and μ is a multiplicity. In modern terms:
- If f_K̃ specializes to a point of U_s, the composite is trivial.
- If it specializes to the cusp i, the composite is, up to conjugacy, the loop around cusp i raised to the order of contact μ.

Since the image of I is normal in the image of E_K̃, the decomposition group E_K̃ maps into the normalizer of L_i=K_i(T) in E_{U_Õ}. That is, the specialized section is a 'cuspidal' section at cusp i.

The next page identifies the bottom row with the fundamental group extension of the special fibre U_s over k(s). It then studies the induced lifting E_K̃→E_{U_Õ}≅E_{U_s}. This is a local analysis of how sections, and in particular sections coming from points, specialize at codimension-one points. It serves the section conjecture and its relative or birational variants (the 'Longue Marche' circle of ideas, 1981).
errors: The identification I_{s'}≅T, and the existence of a loop homomorphism T→π, requires residue characteristic 0 or passing to the tame/prime-to-p quotient. Otherwise the full inertia is not procyclic and π is not the right group in the special fibre. Grothendieck is implicitly in characteristic 0 or tame.

The formula K_i∘(μ·id_T) is stated loosely ('essentiellement'). It holds only up to conjugation in π and assumes μ≠0. For μ=0 (point specializing into U_s) the map is trivial and no normalizer statement follows.

Strictly, the image of E_K̃ normalizes μ·L_i. One needs the standard fact that in π (a free or surface profinite group) the normalizer of an open subgroup of a cuspidal inertia group equals the normalizer of L_i. This is true but not stated.

ideas.what: 3×3 diagram comparing the fundamental group extensions of U over the henselian fraction field and over the henselian DVR. The kernel of the vertical map is identified with the inertia group ≅T via the snake lemma.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of the fundamental group extension / homotopy exact sequence over a henselian DVR
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (Grothendieck) for the specialization theory; standard in the anabelian literature (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Stix)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 exp. X–XIII for the specialization/tame theory, though not in this exact diagram form

ideas.what: A rational point specializing to a cusp gives a section whose restriction to inertia is conjugate to the cuspidal loop raised to the order of contact. Hence the decomposition group lands in the normalizer of a cuspidal inertia group.
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal sections / packets of cuspidal sections; local behaviour of sections at cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Nakamura (decomposition groups at cusps, 1990s), S. Mochizuki, J. Stix ('Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups', 2013)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in the 1983 letter to Faltings, which discusses points at infinity and sections; unsure of explicit statement

ideas.what: Restricting the section attached to a K-point to the decomposition group at a codimension-one point gives the section of the K̃-point; reduction then yields a lifting into E_{U_s}.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of sections / functoriality of the section map along henselization

missed.claim: An early (c. 1981) explicit formulation by Grothendieck of the local cuspidal behaviour of sections under specialization at codimension-one points of a higher-dimensional base: inertia maps via μ·(cuspidal loop), and the decomposition group goes into the normalizer of the cuspidal inertia. This anticipates the 'cuspidal section' analysis later developed by Nakamura and Stix. The mathematics itself is now standard.
missed.quote: on a un [composé] essentiellement par un K_i∘(μ,id_T), où K_i : T→π est un homo.-lacets, relatif à l'indice i. Ainsi le groupe de décomposition E_K̃ s'envoie dans le normalisateur de L_i = K_i(T)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents that Grothendieck had the cuspidal-section mechanism in mind in the Longue Marche notes. No new mathematical content for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine local computation (snake lemma plus tame specialization at cusps) that is now standard in anabelian geometry. It is of historical interest as an early instance of cuspidal-section reasoning, but nothing a specialist would find unknown.
transcription_corrections: 'I_s ≃ I_{s'}≃T' in the diagram: the left entry is likely just 'I' (the kernel of E_{U_K̃}→E_{U_Õ}), written with a heavy stroke.
The vertical labels on the right are 'Gal(K̄/K̃)' and 'Gal(k̄/k)', attached by '≃' to E_K̃ and E_Õ respectively.
'Les sections ... n'est autre' should read 'n'est autre / ne sont autres que'; '(elles-mêmes définies par les pts K-rat. f_K de U_K sur K)'.

'Si on compose avec E_{U_K̃}→E_{U_õ} envoie I≃T dans π, on a un commutant' probably reads 'Si on compose avec E_{U_K̃}→E_{U_õ} [qui] envoie I≃T dans π, on a un composé [qui s'exprime] essentiellement par ...'.
'K_i∘(μ, id_T)' is plausibly 'K_i∘(μ·id_T)' (multiplication by the multiplicity μ).
